summary: OrbitPay: sustained streaming stalls and duplicate completions during payment confirmations — major escalation and post-incident action plan
description:
Issue summary: Between ~2026-02-25T01:15:00Z and 2026-02-25T03:10:00Z OrbitPay experienced repeated streaming stalls (clients received truncated or paused server-sent streams) and duplicate final completions for payment confirmation flows. Impact: merchant confirmation endpoints intermittently produced duplicate events, causing client retries and risk of double-charging. Customer escalated immediately due to live transactions failing.

Initial impact estimate: ~3% of streaming requests in the US-East population; severity high because paths touch payment confirmation flows. Incident declared P0 and escalated to on-call SRE and Support leadership.

Observed behaviour: streams cut mid-response (no terminal DONE frame), client reconnects and receives the completion again; spikes in streaming-reset metric and 5xx for streaming endpoints. Tail latency (p99) for streaming endpoints increased by ~340ms during peak.

Relevant external references: internal Slack thread #support (link: slack://channel/support/archives/p0123xxxxx), status page incident ID incident-20260225-orbitpay.

Customer communication summary: initial acknowledgment within first response SLA; bridge call with OrbitPay product and engineering teams held 2026-02-25 02:30 UTC. Regular status updates provided every 20 minutes during mitigation window.
steps_to_reproduce: Invoke /v1/chat/stream with OrbitPay production API key and a payment-confirmation prompt payload (~1.2k tokens) under sustained load (~250-400 rps).
Observe client receives partial stream chunks then silence (>10s) without DONE frame, client reconnects and final completion is returned again (duplicate).
Reproduce probability increases when server-side concurrent KV-cache hits and kernel-selection churn occur (observed during rolling deployment).
logs: 2026-02-25T01:16:05Z router-abc123 WARN stream-reset session_id=ox-19 reason=client-silence source=serving-runtime
2026-02-25T01:16:07Z runtime-xyx987 ERROR kvcache-mismatch shard=5 request=0x23fa4 error=cache-corruption-detected
2026-02-25T01:22:49Z router-abc123 WARN backpressure high conn_pool=us-east pool_util=0.94
2026-02-25T02:05:11Z observability INFO alert firing=streaming-resets threshold=5m window=1m value=62
investigation_notes: Triage: SRE validated elevated streaming-reset and duplicate-completion counters aligned with OrbitPay requests (prod-us-east).
Hypothesis 1: KV-cache shard drift during a kernel-selection/rolling update caused inconsistent prefix state; reconnects re-evaluated prefixes and emitted final completion twice.

Hypothesis 2: Router session affinity mismatch after a partial rollout of PR #2987 introduced a window where streaming connections lost their server-side session marker and were reattached to a new runtime which replayed final completions.
Telemetry: tracing shows same request_id served by two different runtime instances for ~45s windows; KV cache mismatch logs present in same timeframe.
Reproduction: load test with controlled kernel-selection churn reproduced truncated streams and duplicate completions locally; disabling the canary rollout removed the duplication in test cluster.

Root cause (determined): a regression in the serving runtime's backpressure and session-resume logic introduced in runtime PR #2987 that, under high concurrency and during kernel selection, could drop the stream terminal event and allow a replay path on reconnect.

Contributing factors: rolling deployment timing, higher-than-expected concurrency from OrbitPay during a scheduled marketing event, and insufficient early-warning telemetry for session-affinity drift.
mitigation_and_timeline: 2026-02-25 02:40 UTC: Scoped mitigation - increased router sticky-session timeout and applied temporary connection backpressure cap for OrbitPay token bucket.
2026-02-25 03:10 UTC: Hotfix rollout - reverted runtime PR #2987 on prod-us-east and disabled ongoing canary. Immediate reduction observed in duplicate completions and stream resets.
2026-02-25 03:45 UTC: Full rollback completed and monitoring confirmed normalization of streaming metrics by 04:00 UTC.
2026-02-25 05:00 UTC: Customer update: OrbitPay confirmed reduced failures and resumed normal operations; Offer of invoice credit and support-led replay audit initiated.
resolution:
Root cause fix: revert of runtime PR #2987 and patch backported with improved session-resume checks that ensure terminal events are idempotent. Patch deployed to prod-us-east 2026-02-25 03:10 UTC; follow-up verification completed 2026-02-25 04:15 UTC.

Customer remediation: Applied proactive reconciliation support for OrbitPay transactions during the incident window; finance and CS coordinated an invoice credit for impacted transactions (agreement logged).

Preventative actions (post-incident):
- Add kernel-selection and session-affinity end-to-end tests to the CI harness.
- Introduce an alert for 'tracing:request_id_seen_on_multiple_runtimes' to catch session splits earlier.
- Tighten canary rollout gating for backpressure or session-related changes.
- Run a targeted capacity burn test ahead of known OrbitPay traffic spikes; publish guidance to customers for planned marketing events.

Follow-ups assigned and due dates: INT-4411 (engineering postmortem) assigned to SRE team, due 2026-03-04; SUP-772000 (customer compensation and audit) assigned to CS, due 2026-03-01.
